rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so there is no evidence yet about whether RNA, image, aggregation, or fusion drives validation performance. This experiment tests a minimal RNA-only baseline using a single profile and PCA, clarifying whether basic RNA representation alone provides useful signal. It is the best first use of budget because it establishes a simple reference point for later comparisons of RNA encoders, multiprofile aggregation, image-only models, and multimodal fusion without introducing unnecessary complexity.

The only completed experiment is an RNA-only, single-profile PCA baseline, so the largest remaining uncertainty is whether the image modality provides useful signal at all. config_010 tests an image-only, single-profile ResNet50 model, keeping the profile setting simple and avoiding fusion or aggregation changes. This is the best next experiment because it isolates the effect of modality before adding multimodal fusion or more complex image encoders, helping determine whether future budget should focus on RNA, image, or multimodal configurations.

The only strong unimodal evidence so far is RNA-only with PCA and singleprofile, which substantially outperforms image-only ResNet in both accuracy and F1. The key uncertainty is whether using multiple profiles with a simple aggregation can improve on the best RNA baseline. config_002 tests this by extending the promising PCA RNA setting to multiprofile with avgpool, the simplest aggregation option, before trying more complex choices like transformer aggregation or multimodal fusion. This is an efficient next step because it exploits the strongest current direction while isolating the effect of profile aggregation with minimal added complexity.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile RNA with PCA and avgpool (config_002) improves substantially over singleprofile RNA (config_001), while image-only ResNet is weak. The main uncertainty is whether a more expressive aggregation method can further improve multiprofile RNA. config_003 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer, directly testing this while preserving the current best model setting, profile setting, and RNA encoder. This is an efficient exploitation step: if it improves, it identifies a better aggregation for later encoder or fusion extensions; if not, it shows avgpool is sufficient and avoids unnecessary complexity.

Existing evidence shows RNA is much stronger than image, and multiprofile avgpool with PCA improves RNA accuracy and F1 over single-profile and transformer aggregation. The key uncertainty is whether a learned RNA encoder can improve the current best RNA-only baseline. config_005 keeps the best profile/aggregation setting (multiprofile + avgpool) and only changes the RNA encoder from PCA to scvi_n200, directly testing representation quality. This is a clean, high-value extension: if it improves, it identifies a promising RNA encoder; if not, it supports PCA as sufficient before adding more complex image or fusion changes.

RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool is the strongest evidence so far, and scvi_n200 reaches the best validation accuracy/F1, but that is a single experiment and scgpt is still untested. config_008 keeps the promising multiprofile/avgpool setting and changes only the RNA encoder, isolating the effect of representation. This is the best next use of budget because it reduces uncertainty about whether scvi is truly the best RNA representation or whether scgpt can improve further, without adding multimodal complexity or changing multiple design choices at once.

The strongest completed result is config_005, RNA-only with multiprofile, scvi_n200, and avgpool aggregation, with validation accuracy 0.650 and F1 0.628. Avgpool has also outperformed transformer for PCA multiprofile RNA, but it is unclear whether the stronger scvi representation might benefit from transformer aggregation. config_006 keeps the best encoder and profile setting fixed and changes only aggregation, cleanly testing the aggregation choice. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising direction while reducing uncertainty about an important design decision before moving to more complex multimodal fusion.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile models, especially scvi_n200 with avgpool/transformer, are much stronger than single-profile RNA, while image-only single-profile ResNet50 is weak. The key uncertainty is whether the weak image result is due to single-profile representation or inherent lack of image signal. config_011 tests the same ResNet50 encoder with multiprofile avgpool, mirroring the RNA design that improved performance, and provides a clean image-only baseline for later fusion. It is the best next step because it reduces uncertainty about profile/aggregation for image without confounding a new image encoder or jumping to multimodal fusion.

RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 is the strongest evidence so far (avgpool 0.650, transformer 0.653), while image-only resnet50 is much weaker (single 0.208, multiprofile avgpool 0.328). The key uncertainty is whether adding image features can improve the strong RNA-only model. config_031 keeps the well-supported scvi_n200/multiprofile/avgpool settings and uses the already characterized resnet50 image encoder, so it mainly tests the effect of adding image plus fusion. Weighted fusion is a logical first multimodal test because the modalities are imbalanced; it can clarify whether adaptive fusion can exploit image signal without letting the weak image stream dominate. This is more informative than changing image encoder or aggregation simultaneously and has high expected value relative to the current RNA-only best.

The only multimodal result so far (config_031) is the best configuration, but it is based on a single experiment and uses weighted fusion. RNA-only results show scvi_n200 with multiprofile is strong, while image-only models are weak, so it is unclear whether the multimodal gain comes from image information generally or specifically from weighted fusion. config_030 keeps the same model, profile, encoders, and aggregation as config_031 but changes only fusion from weighted to concat, isolating the fusion effect. This is the most efficient next test because it clarifies whether the best multimodal result is robust before investing in more complex multimodal variants.
